title: Nearest, measured in dollars
hook: Which person is nearest to you: a 31-year-old or a 60-year-old?

knows: that nearest-neighbour methods find the most similar example by distance
doesNotKnow: that the units of each feature decide which feature dominates distance
that features are rescaled before distance-based methods

misconception: 'Nearest' means nearest in every way that matters, regardless of how each feature is measured.
objective: The learner can explain that straight-line distance is dominated by whichever feature has the biggest numbers, so changing units can change who is nearest, and that features are scaled to comparable ranges first.

claims.text: The toy has 12 invented people plus 'you' (30 years, $50,000); A is 31 and earns $58,000, B is 60 and earns $51,000. Distance is √(age gap² + income gap²), with income in the chosen unit, so on the stage 1 year of age counts like one unit of income ($1, $100 or $1,000).
claims.source: The lesson's own data and distance in Demo.tsx (QUERY, PEOPLE, dist). The ten unlabelled people were placed by hand so that only A or B is ever nearest. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 16): Demo.tsx: QUERY 30/$50,000; PEOPLE has 12 entries (A 31/$58,000, B 60/$51,000, ten unlabelled); dist = hypot(age gap, income gap / unit); header '1 year of age counts like $1 / $100 / $1,000 of income'. node: nearest is B at $1 and $100, A at $1,000; for the stage's three units only A or B is nearest. Advisory: the source's 'only A or B is ever nearest' is too broad: on a 1% grid of units from 1 to 100,000, an unlabelled person is nearest on 83 steps (units the stage does not offer).

claims.text: With income in dollars, B is 1,000.4 away and A is 8,000.0 away, so B is nearest. In $100s B is still nearest (31.6 vs 80.0).
claims.source: √(30² + 1000²) = 1000.45; √(1² + 8000²) = 8000.00; √(30² + 10²) = 31.62; √(1² + 80²) = 80.01. Reproduced by dist() and nearest() from Demo.tsx in node.

claims.text: With income in $1,000s, A is 8.1 away and B is 30.0 away, so A is nearest.
claims.source: √(1² + 8²) = 8.06; √(30² + 1²) = 30.02. Reproduced by dist() and nearest() from Demo.tsx in node; the next nearest person is 10.3 away.

claims.text: Features are put on comparable scales before distance-based methods such as nearest neighbours.
claims.source: Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman 2009, The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., §13.3 (features standardised before nearest-neighbour classification); scikit-learn user guide, 'Preprocessing data' (standardisation).

recall.question: A house-price model finds similar houses by distance on floor area (in square feet, 500 to 5,000) and number of bedrooms (1 to 6), unscaled. Which feature mostly decides 'similar'?
options: Floor area, because its numbers are far bigger
Bedrooms, because they matter more to buyers
recall.why: Unscaled distance is dominated by the feature with the largest numeric spread. A gap of a few hundred square feet swamps a gap of several bedrooms unless the features are rescaled.
